query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a minor amount (around 1–2 at.%) of yttrium to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance at high temperatures by promoting the formation of an adherent, slow-growing yttrium-doped oxide scale, while preserving its good room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy known to exhibit 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C but with inadequate oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Introduce 1–2 at.% of yttrium during alloy processing via vacuum arc melting.
generation.conditions: Oxidation testing in air at 800 °C for 5 hours and mechanical testing at room temperature and up to 1000 °C under strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, adherent yttrium-stabilized oxide scale (likely a modified HfO2 scale doped with Y) that acts as an effective diffusion barrier against oxygen ingress.
generation.mechanism: Yttrium, when added in small amounts, segregates to the oxide–metal interface during high-temperature exposure, enhancing oxide adhesion and slowing oxygen diffusion. This suppresses the rapid oxidation (pesting) seen in untreated alloys, while the bulk microstructure and mechanical properties remain largely unaffected.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the untreated alloy, the yttrium-doped HfNbTaTiZr is expected to show significantly improved oxidation resistance during a 5 h air exposure at 800 °C (e.g., lower weight gain and reduced scale spallation) with no measurable loss in room-temperature tensile ductility or high-temperature yield strength.
generation.baseline: Untreated, equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy that experiences rapid oxidation (pesting) under air exposure at 800 °C, with proven room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies only to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloys processed by vacuum arc melting, under oxidation conditions of 800 °C in air for up to 5 h and mechanical testing conditions at room temperature and 1000 °C with strain rates between 10−4 and 10−2 s−1.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal yttrium concentration for maintaining mechanical properties while improving oxidation resistance is not precisely known and may require further experimental calibration. The potential influence of yttrium on microstructural stability over longer exposures is also uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples: one with 1–2 at.% yttrium addition via vacuum arc melting and one baseline without yttrium. Expose both sets to air at 800 °C for 5 hours. After exposure, characterize the oxide scale using SEM/EDS and measure weight gain. Perform mechanical tests at room temperature and at 1000 °C (strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1) to measure tensile ductility and yield strength.
measurements: SEM/EDS analysis of oxide scale thickness, continuity, and composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yttrium-added samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in oxidation resistance (i.e., similar or higher weight gain or scale degradation) or if their room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength are degraded relative to the untreated baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.

citation_validation.initial_error: generated hypothesis cites unavailable evidence: ['Earlier oxidation-protection research in a related non-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy that prevented pesting at 800 °C for 5 h suggests that reactive element additions can improve oxidation resistance.']
